extracted.intended_audience: senior/key personnel and other significant contributors preparing NIH-style biosketches and grant research support sections
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare an NIH-style biosketch and current/pending support section for senior/key personnel, following the specified format (Personal Statement, Positions, Contributions to Science, Research Support) and page limits. Includes required header fields, education/training table, representative publications, and disclosure of overlap/effort for each award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this template for every Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors; the entire biosketch for each person must not exceed five pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Header fields required
rubrics_metrics.description: NAME; eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login); POSITION TITLE; EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the person's full name, eRA Commons username, current position title, and an education/training table with institution and location, degree (if applicable), completion date (MM/YYYY), and field of study. Begin with baccalaureate and include postdoctoral/residency if applicable; modify rows as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. PERSONAL STATEMENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal statement summarizing the individual's training, research focus, leadership, mentoring record, and relevance to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Personal Statement to describe career-long focus and qualifications, past and ongoing roles (e.g., PI/PD on relevant grants), specific research accomplishments relevant to the application, mentoring experience (number of trainees, mentoring committees served), and willingness/ability to serve on the project's mentoring committee. Provide brief examples of translational or clinical activities if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. POSITIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: List positions (titles and institutional affiliations) with dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a chronological list of employment/appointments with start and end dates and institution/department, including clinical training positions (intern, resident) and academic leadership roles. Include relevant leadership titles (e.g., Director, Vice Chair) and years of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. CONTRIBUTIONS TO SCIENCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbered contributions summarizing major scientific contributions/themes, each accompanied by a brief explanatory paragraph and representative publications (with citations, PMIDs, PMCIDs where available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each contribution, provide a concise description of the scientific area or discovery, its significance, and list representative publications (labelled a, b, c, etc.) including journal citation and PMID/PMCID when available. Use multiple numbered items to cover distinct contributions (the sample shows five).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative publications and links
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide links or listings to publication records (e.g., PubMed, PubMed Central, myNCBI) and include citations/PMIDs in Contributions to Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include URLs to aggregated publication listings (PubMed, PubMed Central, myNCBI) and include PMIDs/PMCIDs for cited representative works to enable reviewers to find the publications easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. RESEARCH SUPPORT (current and pending)
rubrics_metrics.description: List current and pending research support with grant number, project title, funding agency, dates, award type, and role (e.g., PI, Co-Investigator, MPI, Local UW Co-PI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each award include: grant number (e.g., R35 CA197078), PI name in parentheses, agency (NIH/NCI, etc.), project title, role (e.g., Role: PI), performance dates, percent effort or calendar months (e.g., 0.72 Cal Mo), and total project award if shown. Distinguish active vs pending awards and mark institutional/consortium roles when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: State effort/commitment for each award
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide calendar months or percent effort (e.g., 0.72 Cal Mo, 3.0 calendar) for projects listed under current and pending support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report effort consistently (calendar months or fraction FTE) so reviewers can assess workload and potential overlap with the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare overlap and plan if overlapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any budgetary, commitment, or scientific overlap between listed projects and the proposed work and state plans to address overlap (e.g., relinquish one award if both are received).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether there is overlap (e.g., 'There is no budgetary, commitment, or scientific overlap with the work proposed.' or describe the planned relinquishment or mitigation if overlapping awards might be received). Include an 'OVERLAP' subsection indicating 'None' when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role designation clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state the individual's role on each project (e.g., Role: PI; Role: Co-Investigator; Role: Multiple PI; Role: Local UW Co-PI; Role: Collaborator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit role labels for each listed award so reviewers understand leadership and responsibilities. For multi-PI awards, indicate shared roles and project-specific responsibilities when relevant.
